roster.name: Incineroar
roster.rationale: Incineroar is the most role-dense Pokémon in the format: Intimidate cycling, Fake Out pressure, and slow Parting Shot pivoting all on one Fire/Dark chassis. It fits onto virtually any archetype — sun, rain, Trick Room, balance — and its unique combination of disruption and bulk is irreplaceable on this board. At 18 points it's a premium but fair price for the single most proven VGC cornerstone.

roster.name: Mega Metagross
roster.rationale: Mega Metagross (17 pts) is the best Mega still on the board — 80/145/150/105/110/110 with Tough Claws gives both elite bulk and nuclear physical damage. It pairs well with Incineroar: Metagross covers Incineroar's Rock and Fairy weaknesses, while Incineroar's Dark typing handles the Ghost and Dark moves that threaten Metagross. At 110 base Speed it also gives me a fast mode that can set Stealth Rock or go straight offensive, keeping tempo after an Incineroar pivot.

roster.name: Dragapult
roster.rationale: Dragapult (14) fills three urgent needs at once: a blazing-fast special attacker (base 142 Speed, 100 SpA), a Ground immunity via its Ghost typing, and a disruptive support toolkit (Will-O-Wisp, Thunder Wave, screens, U-turn). It pairs beautifully with Incineroar's Intimidate to neuter physical threats and gives me a pivot core that can control tempo. At 14 points it leaves 51 for 7 picks — plenty of budget to chase a dedicated Tailwind setter and a secondary Mega later.

roster.name: Rotom-Wash
roster.rationale: Rotom-Wash is the premier defensive pivot still on the board, giving me a crucial Ground immunity via Levitate that my roster sorely needs. Its Electric/Water typing dominates the emerging rain team (Pelipper, Mega Swampert, Basculegion) and resists sun-boosted Fire from inclusionai's Zard Y, while Volt Switch forms a potent pivoting core with Incineroar's Parting Shot. At 14 points it's excellent value, leaving 37 for 6 picks to round out speed control, a secondary Mega, and a Fairy.

roster.name: Klefki
roster.rationale: Klefki is the last remaining Prankster user with a support movepool this deep — priority Thunder Wave, Reflect, Light Screen, Spikes, and even Trick Room all at +1. Steel/Fairy typing patches my Dark and Dragon weaknesses while stacking beautifully with Incineroar's Intimidate and Rotom-Wash's bulk. At 11 points it leaves 26 for five more picks, keeping a secondary Mega and a dedicated Tailwind setter (Corviknight or Noivern) well within reach.

roster.name: Corviknight
roster.rationale: Corviknight (13) is the ideal Tailwind setter for this roster — a bulky Steel/Flying pivot with Roost, U-turn, and Mirror Armor that adds a crucial Ground immunity alongside Rotom-W's Levitate. It rounds out the defensive core beautifully: Incineroar + Metagross + Rotom-W + Corviknight + Klefki covers each other's weaknesses well, and Tailwind gives Dragapult and Metagross a fast mode beyond Klefki's Thunder Wave/Trick Room. At 13 points it leaves 13 for the final 4 picks, which is tight but workable with budget special attackers like Chandelure (6), Gengar (8), or Gardevoir (10).

roster.name: Serperior
roster.rationale: Serperior (5 pts) fills a critical gap: I have zero Grass coverage against the rain team's Mega Swampert, Basculegion, Feraligatr, and Primarina. Contrary Leaf Storm turns it into a snowball special win condition, 113 base Speed outruns most of the format, and Glare provides speed control that hits Ground-types (unlike Klefki's Thunder Wave). At 5 points it's excellent value, leaving 8 points for my final 3 picks.

roster.name: Gliscor
roster.rationale: Gliscor (3) fills the glaring Ground-type gap in my roster — I currently have zero Ground coverage into Gholdengo, Aegislash, and Archaludon. Poison Heal makes it a status-absorbing defensive pivot that synergises perfectly with my Steel-heavy core (Mega Metagross, Klefki, Corviknight), while its Electric immunity protects Rotom-Wash from Volt Switch spam. At 95 base Speed it outspeeds most defensive mons and can run Toxic/Roost/Earthquake/Protect sets that my bulky offense desperately needs.

roster.name: Clawitzer
roster.rationale: Clawitzer (4 pts) is the ideal special wallbreaker for this roster. Mega Launcher boosts Water Pulse, Dark Pulse, Aura Sphere, and Dragon Pulse to 90–127 BP off 120 base SpA, giving me SE coverage into Steels (Aura Sphere), Ghosts/Dragons (Dark/Dragon Pulse), and Fires (Water Pulse). It also brings Flip Turn for pivoting and rounds out my special attacking core alongside Dragapult and Rotom-Wash. Leaves exactly 1 point for Dedenne as the final pick.

roster.name: Furfrou
roster.rationale: Dedenne is already drafted by Luna-pro, so the private note's plan is void. Furfrou is the best remaining 1-point option: Fur Coat doubles its physical Defense, making it a legitimate bulky pivot at base 102 Speed. It brings Thunder Wave for speed control, U-turn for momentum, and a Ghost immunity that helps against Mega Gengar and Dragapult — unique utility none of the other 1-point leftovers can match.

roster.name: Meowscarada
roster.rationale: Meowscarada is the premier Chlorophyll sweeper available and thrives directly under Drought from Mega Charizard Y. At 12 points it's above my per-pick average but well worth it—Protean plus Chlorophyll-boosted Grass STAB in sun gives it terrifying offensive presence, and its Grass/Dark typing covers two of the types my Fire/Flying core is neutral or weak to.

roster.name: Torkoal
roster.rationale: Torkoal is a premier sun team defensive pivot. With Drought, it provides permanent sun backup when Mega Charizard Y is benched, and its massive 140 Defense plus Shell Armor makes it a reliable physical wall. It slots perfectly into the sun core alongside Mega Charizard Y and Meowscarada's Chlorophyll speed.

roster.name: Toxapex
roster.rationale: Toxapex is the premier defensive Water-type still on the board. Its monstrous 152/142 defensive stats combined with Regenerator make it an incredibly durable pivot that walls a huge portion of the physical meta. It fills the 'bulky Water for defensive coverage' slot identified in my notes and pairs well with the sun core—opponents can't easily break through it to threaten Charizard Y or Venusaur. At 8 points it's reasonable value, leaving 32 points for 5 remaining slots.

roster.name: Aegislash
roster.rationale: Aegislash is the highest-impact available pick for my sun team. Steel/Ghost with Stance Change and King's Shield provides both a second offensive threat and crucial team support, deterring contact moves against my Fire core. Its excellent defensive typing covers Normal, Flying, Rock, Bug, Steel, Grass, Psychic, Dragon, Ice, Poison, and Fighting — shoring up many of my team's weaknesses.

roster.name: Skarmory
roster.rationale: Skarmory at 3 points is the most budget-efficient way to cover two critical team needs: hazard removal via Defog and speed control via Tailwind/Icy Wind. It also sets Spikes and provides Roost for longevity. At 3 points it leaves 15 for three remaining picks. The Fire weakness is manageable by protecting Skarmory and using Aegislash Shield form to absorb Fire hits.

roster.name: Swampert
roster.rationale: Swampert at 6 points is the most efficient Ground-type pivot still available. Water/Ground typing gives me crucial Electric immunity to protect Charizard and Torkoal, while providing excellent coverage alongside my Sun core. It can run U-turn for momentum, Stealth Rock, Earthquake, and Ice Beam, filling the team's biggest remaining hole.

roster.name: Spiritomb
roster.rationale: Spiritomb (Ghost/Dark, 6 pts) is the best available special wall and directly addresses the Psychic/Ghost/Dark coverage gap. Its 108/108 special defenses, Pressure for PP stall, and Infiltrator to bypass screens make it a premier pick. It resists Psychic, Ghost, and Dark, and is immune to Normal and Fighting—covering key threats from Farigiraf, Mega Gengar, Dragapult, and Hatterene. Leaves 3 points for Scrafty as a Fighting/Dark physical attacker with Moxie and Intimidate.

roster.name: Mega Gengar
roster.rationale: Mega Gengar with Shadow Tag is the most uniquely powerful entry on the board — trapping prevents opposing switches, which is game-winning in doubles. At 18 points it's elite value, leaving 82 for 9 remaining picks (~9 avg). No other available Pokémon replicates Shadow Tag, making it irreplaceable if another coach grabs it before pick 10.

roster.name: Grimmsnarl
roster.rationale: With Whimsicott and Farigiraf both already gone, Grimmsnarl is the last premium Prankster Tailwind user on the board and is essential support for Mega Gengar's speed control and fragility. Prankster screens + Taunt + Tailwind gives Mega Gengar the setup it needs to trap and eliminate key threats. At 16 points it's fairly priced for irreplaceable utility that multiple coaches will want.

roster.name: Tyranitar
roster.rationale: Tyranitar at 14 is exceptional value, filling three needs at once: Sand Stream weather setter, premier physical attacker (134 base Attack), and a bulky Rock/Dark defensive backbone that gets a SpD boost in its own sand. It costs 4 fewer points than Pelipper while being a far stronger standalone Pokémon, and it opens a Sand Rush Excadrill (13) core for later rounds. Sand also chips opposing teams and can override P2's sun or P5's potential rain.

roster.name: Excadrill
roster.rationale: Excadrill completes the sand core with Tyranitar's Sand Stream, giving me a fast Ground/Steel sweeper under Sand Rush that threatens the Fire, Steel, and Electric types across opponent rosters. At 13 points it's excellent value and likely to be grabbed by another coach soon, especially with sand setters like Hippowdon still on the board. The Steel typing also adds a much-needed Fairy and Dragon resist to my roster.

roster.name: Gholdengo
roster.rationale: Gholdengo at 16 points is the best-value elite pick left on the board and fills my critical special-attacker slot perfectly. Steel/Ghost typing is immune to sandstorm damage, synergizes with my TTar+Excadrill core, and Good as Gold shuts down status moves from opposing Whimsicott, Grimmsnarl mirrors, and Sinistcha. With 23 points remaining for 5 picks I can still afford a budget Intimidate user like Krookodile (9) or Staraptor (10) next round.

roster.name: Paldean Tauros Aqua
roster.rationale: Fills two needs in one 9-pt slot: Intimidate (priority #1) and Water typing (priority #2). Fighting/Water is unique on my team and patches the Water weakness that P5's rain core exploits. Gets Close Combat, Wave Crash, Aqua Jet priority, and Rock Slide for spread damage. 100 base Spe and 105 base Def make it a solid Intimidate pivot that doesn't stack weaknesses with my existing Dark/Ghost-heavy core.

roster.name: Vaporeon
roster.rationale: Vaporeon's Water Absorb is critical insurance for Tyranitar (4x Water weak) and Excadrill (2x Water weak), especially against P5's rain core and P3's Milotic. Wish + Protect gives team healing that keeps my sand core healthy, and Ice Beam threatens the Garchomp and Dragonite running around. At 5 points it leaves exactly 3 for two final picks, where 1-pt options like Absol (Sucker Punch priority) or Houndoom (Flash Fire) can round out the bench.

roster.name: Mega Floette
roster.rationale: Mega Floette is an elite win condition and support-resistant special attacker: Fairy Aura amplifies its already exceptional 155 Special Attack, while 148 Special Defense gives it unusually reliable field presence. Its Fairy typing also offers immediate counterplay into the drafted Mega Gengar and keeps us flexible around the emerging sun and Intimidate cores.

roster.name: Garchomp
roster.rationale: Garchomp is the cleanest complementary centerpiece beside Mega Floette: it pressures Fire-, Steel-, and Poison-types, notably threatening Mega Charizard Y with Rock Slide and Mega Gengar with Ground coverage. Floette in return checks opposing Dragons and Fighting pressure that can target Garchomp, while Garchomp's immediate speed and physical damage give the roster needed offensive balance.

roster.name: Milotic
roster.rationale: Milotic is an efficient defensive pivot that directly punishes the Intimidate-heavy teams already forming, especially Incineroar, via Competitive. It also gives this roster valuable Water coverage, Icy Wind speed control, and a sturdy special-defense backbone beside Mega Floette and Garchomp.

roster.name: Talonflame
roster.rationale: Talonflame supplies the proactive Tailwind the roster lacks, while Gale Wings also lets it threaten a faster priority Taunt into opposing Whimsicott before it can establish its own speed control. Its Fire/Flying pressure gives Floette and Garchomp a useful Steel-checking partner, particularly into Mega Metagross and Archaludon structures.

roster.name: Hatterene
roster.rationale: Hatterene gives this roster a credible Trick Room mode and, just as importantly, a way to reverse opposing Trick Room from Farigiraf/Sinistcha or Torkoal compositions. Magic Bounce provides valuable counterplay into status and disruption while its Fairy/Psychic pressure complements Garchomp, Milotic, and Talonflame well.

roster.name: Manectric
roster.rationale: At 1 point, Manectric is an exceptional efficiency pick: Lightning Rod gives the roster a real Water/Electric redirection option into the rain core, while its 105 base Speed and access to disruption let it contribute outside that matchup. It preserves 23 points for four slots, enough to still add a sturdy Steel/Poison answer and matchup-specific utility.

roster.name: Metagross
roster.rationale: Metagross is exceptional value at 6 points and gives this roster its needed Steel-type defensive backbone into opposing Fairy pressure, especially Primarina, Grimmsnarl, and potential Mega Floette mirrors. Clear Body also makes it a reliable answer into the league’s many Intimidate users, while Bullet Punch provides valuable priority for the fast offensive matchups.

roster.name: Hisuian Goodra
roster.rationale: Hisuian Goodra is an exceptional 6-point fit: its Steel/Dragon typing and 150 base SpD give the roster a durable special pivot that complements the physically sturdy Garchomp, Metagross, and Milotic. Sap Sipper also creates a valuable Grass immunity for the Water- and Ground-oriented core, while it remains usable in either Tailwind or Trick Room compositions.

roster.name: Scrafty
roster.rationale: Scrafty gives the roster a vital cheap VGC utility package in Intimidate, Fake Out, and Dark/Fighting coverage, while functioning well under either Talonflame Tailwind or Hatterene Trick Room. It also helps our Steel- and Psychic-heavy core into Ghost- and Dark-type pressure without committing our primary Mega choice.

roster.name: Mega Alakazam
roster.rationale: Mega Alakazam supplies the fast special offense the roster otherwise lacks, with 150 base Speed, 175 base Special Attack, and Trace creating strong matchup-specific utility. It also gives the team a legitimate alternate Mega option to Mega Floette, while Talonflame/Scrafty and Hatterene preserve flexible Tailwind and Trick Room modes.

roster.name: Archaludon
roster.rationale: Archaludon is the strongest remaining high-end anchor and gives the roster immediate Steel/Dragon defensive value against Mega Floette, while Stamina lets it scale naturally in doubles. Its excellent mixed offenses, broad weather compatibility, and access to strong positioning tools make it a reliable centerpiece rather than a matchup-dependent specialist.

roster.name: Farigiraf
roster.rationale: Farigiraf directly supports Archaludon with Trick Room and Helping Hand while Armor Tail blocks priority, giving the roster a strong alternate speed mode. Its Normal typing also grants immunity to Mega Gengar’s Ghost attacks, and it provides valuable counterplay against opposing priority and weather-based offensive teams without committing us to rain that would empower Basculegion.

roster.name: Sinistcha
roster.rationale: Sinistcha adds valuable redirection, Hospitality healing, and a second Trick Room option without introducing rain that would empower opposing Basculegion. Its Grass/Ghost typing helps pressure Water- and Ground-types while providing a Ghost immunity, and Heatproof gives it useful counterplay into the opposing sun structures. This also leaves enough budget to fill the remaining slots with cheaper speed, Dark/Fairy answers, and offensive pieces.

roster.name: Sneasler
roster.rationale: Sneasler directly supplies the Fighting/Poison pressure this core lacks, threatening opposing Dark- and Fairy-types while complementing Farigiraf’s Armor Tail with fast disruption such as Taunt, Fake Out, and Coaching. Unburden gives the roster a strong speed-mode option independent of weather, and its 19-point cost still leaves exactly 26 points for six inexpensive depth picks.

roster.name: Armarouge
roster.rationale: Armarouge gives the roster valuable Fire coverage against opposing Steel, Grass, and Ice threats while adding a second credible Trick Room mode alongside Farigiraf. Its access to Wide Guard, Expanding Force, Armor Cannon, and potential Flash Fire utility makes it flexible in both slow and mid-speed compositions. At 8 points, it preserves 18 points for five inexpensive support and matchup picks.

roster.name: Mamoswine
roster.rationale: Mamoswine adds immediate physical Ice/Ground pressure against the many Dragon, Electric, Fire, and Steel threats remaining on the board, while giving the roster a strong Trick Room-compatible attacker alongside Armarouge and Farigiraf. Its Ground typing also gives useful Electric immunity and complements Archaludon’s Steel/Dragon profile without committing to another weather mode. At 12 points, it leaves 6 points for four final picks, requiring a disciplined group of low-cost role players.

roster.name: Altaria
roster.rationale: Altaria is an excellent one-point utility pick: Cloud Nine directly disrupts both the opposing rain core and the sun roster, while Tailwind, Helping Hand, Haze, and Perish Song give it several viable support modes. Its Dragon/Flying typing also provides a Ground immunity for Archaludon and Sneasler, improving positioning without committing the team to a single speed mode.

roster.name: Meowstic-Female
roster.rationale: Meowstic-Female gives the roster unusually valuable low-cost flexibility: Fake Out, Prankster-independent utility, Trick Room, Helping Hand, dual screens, Thunder Wave, and Yawn. It complements both Farigiraf/Armarouge slower modes and Altaria/Sneasler faster modes while adding a second strong support Psychic without consuming a Mega slot.

roster.name: Qwilfish
roster.rationale: Qwilfish is the best remaining 2-point utility pick: Intimidate adds valuable physical control to a roster that otherwise lacks it, while Water/Poison patches several defensive gaps and gives useful disruption through options such as Taunt, Haze, and Nuzzle. Its decent Speed also lets it function as an active support piece rather than passive Intimidate fodder, and it can pressure the opposing rain core with Poison STAB.

roster.name: Dedenne
roster.rationale: Dedenne is the best remaining 1-point fit, providing fast Nuzzle speed control, Electric/Fairy typing, and useful disruption alongside Qwilfish. Its support utility gives the roster another way to pressure faster teams without competing for the Mega slot or duplicating a major offensive role.

roster.name: Whimsicott
roster.rationale: Securing Whimsicott for 19 points gives us elite Prankster utility, Tailwind setup, and Moonblast offense while leaving us with 81 points for our remaining 9 picks. It pairs exceptionally well with heavy hitters and restricted/mega anchors, and keeps a premier speed-control option out of opponents' hands early in the snake draft.

roster.name: Basculegion-Male
roster.rationale: Since Archaludon was already taken, Basculegion-Male is an elite offensive pivot that thrives under Whimsicott's Prankster Tailwind, threatening massive Adaptability-boosted Wave Slashes and Last Respects in the late game. Its Water/Ghost typing and great offensive stats punish many common switch-ins while immediately applying heavy pressure against early draft cores. This leaves us with 62 points for our remaining 8 picks, leaving ample room for a top-tier Mega evolution and strong defensive/support anchors.

roster.name: Pelipper
roster.rationale: Drafting Pelipper provides automatic Drizzle to power up Basculegion-Male's Water-type attacks and Swift Swim capability, creating an immediate rain archetype core alongside Whimsicott. It also secures a strong weather control option for 18 points, leaving 44 points for 7 remaining picks while preserving flexibility for a premier Mega evolution.

roster.name: Mega Swampert
roster.rationale: With Pelipper establishing permanent rain, Mega Swampert is an elite Swift Swim physical sweeper that abuses the weather and rounds out our offensive core. Its Water/Ground typing and huge 150 Attack stat fit seamlessly alongside our existing rain attackers while keeping our budget healthy. This secures our crucial Mega evolution slot with high synergy.

roster.name: Feraligatr
roster.rationale: Feraligatr is an extremely budget-friendly physical threat (cost: 3) that synergizes well with our Rain core through Sheer Force, boosting moves like Liquidation and Ice Fang. It provides powerful offensive backup without straining our remaining points, leaving us with 26 points for our final 5 picks.

roster.name: Primarina
roster.rationale: Primarina provides exceptional defensive utility under rain with its Water/Fairy typing, high Special Defense, and Liquid Voice spread pressure. It covers Dragon and Dark threats while leaving 11 points for our final 4 picks to secure supporting pivots.

roster.name: Forretress
roster.rationale: Forretress costs just 1 point, leaving 10 points for the final 3 picks, and provides invaluable steel utility, hazard stacking, and physical bulk to support the rain team.

roster.name: Mega Ampharos

roster.rationale: We need to use our remaining 6 points across our final 2 picks, spending 5 points here on Alakazam (5) to add a fast special attacker/utility threat, leaving 1 point for our final selection. Alakazam provides incredible speed and high Special Attack to complement our rain core.

Toxapex is the premier defensive Water-type still on the board. Its monstrous 152/142 defensive stats combined with Regenerator make it an incredibly durable pivot that walls a huge portion of the physical meta. It fills the 'bulky Water for defensive coverage' slot identified in my notes and pairs well with the sun core—opponents can't easily break through it to threaten Charizard Y or Venusaur. At 8 points it's reasonable value, leaving 32 points for 5 remaining slots.

Gholdengo at 16 points is the best-value elite pick left on the board and fills my critical special-attacker slot perfectly. Steel/Ghost typing is immune to sandstorm damage, synergizes with my TTar+Excadrill core, and Good as Gold shuts down status moves from opposing Whimsicott, Grimmsnarl mirrors, and Sinistcha. With 23 points remaining for 5 picks I can still afford a budget Intimidate user like Krookodile (9) or Staraptor (10) next round.

Hatterene gives this roster a credible Trick Room mode and, just as importantly, a way to reverse opposing Trick Room from Farigiraf/Sinistcha or Torkoal compositions. Magic Bounce provides valuable counterplay into status and disruption while its Fairy/Psychic pressure complements Garchomp, Milotic, and Talonflame well.

Armarouge gives the roster valuable Fire coverage against opposing Steel, Grass, and Ice threats while adding a second credible Trick Room mode alongside Farigiraf. Its access to Wide Guard, Expanding Force, Armor Cannon, and potential Flash Fire utility makes it flexible in both slow and mid-speed compositions. At 8 points, it preserves 18 points for five inexpensive support and matchup picks.

Feraligatr is an extremely budget-friendly physical threat (cost: 3) that synergizes well with our Rain core through Sheer Force, boosting moves like Liquidation and Ice Fang. It provides powerful offensive backup without straining our remaining points, leaving us with 26 points for our final 5 picks.

Primarina provides exceptional defensive utility under rain with its Water/Fairy typing, high Special Defense, and Liquid Voice spread pressure. It covers Dragon and Dark threats while leaving 11 points for our final 4 picks to secure supporting pivots.

Mamoswine adds immediate physical Ice/Ground pressure against the many Dragon, Electric, Fire, and Steel threats remaining on the board, while giving the roster a strong Trick Room-compatible attacker alongside Armarouge and Farigiraf. Its Ground typing also gives useful Electric immunity and complements Archaludon’s Steel/Dragon profile without committing to another weather mode. At 12 points, it leaves 6 points for four final picks, requiring a disciplined group of low-cost role players.

At 1 point, Manectric is an exceptional efficiency pick: Lightning Rod gives the roster a real Water/Electric redirection option into the rain core, while its 105 base Speed and access to disruption let it contribute outside that matchup. It preserves 23 points for four slots, enough to still add a sturdy Steel/Poison answer and matchup-specific utility.

Fills two needs in one 9-pt slot: Intimidate (priority #1) and Water typing (priority #2). Fighting/Water is unique on my team and patches the Water weakness that P5's rain core exploits. Gets Close Combat, Wave Crash, Aqua Jet priority, and Rock Slide for spread damage. 100 base Spe and 105 base Def make it a solid Intimidate pivot that doesn't stack weaknesses with my existing Dark/Ghost-heavy core.

Aegislash is the highest-impact available pick for my sun team. Steel/Ghost with Stance Change and King's Shield provides both a second offensive threat and crucial team support, deterring contact moves against my Fire core. Its excellent defensive typing covers Normal, Flying, Rock, Bug, Steel, Grass, Psychic, Dragon, Ice, Poison, and Fighting — shoring up many of my team's weaknesses.

Corviknight (13) is the ideal Tailwind setter for this roster — a bulky Steel/Flying pivot with Roost, U-turn, and Mirror Armor that adds a crucial Ground immunity alongside Rotom-W's Levitate. It rounds out the defensive core beautifully: Incineroar + Metagross + Rotom-W + Corviknight + Klefki covers each other's weaknesses well, and Tailwind gives Dragapult and Metagross a fast mode beyond Klefki's Thunder Wave/Trick Room. At 13 points it leaves 13 for the final 4 picks, which is tight but workable with budget special attackers like Chandelure (6), Gengar (8), or Gardevoir (10).

Serperior (5 pts) fills a critical gap: I have zero Grass coverage against the rain team's Mega Swampert, Basculegion, Feraligatr, and Primarina. Contrary Leaf Storm turns it into a snowball special win condition, 113 base Speed outruns most of the format, and Glare provides speed control that hits Ground-types (unlike Klefki's Thunder Wave). At 5 points it's excellent value, leaving 8 points for my final 3 picks.

Skarmory at 3 points is the most budget-efficient way to cover two critical team needs: hazard removal via Defog and speed control via Tailwind/Icy Wind. It also sets Spikes and provides Roost for longevity. At 3 points it leaves 15 for three remaining picks. The Fire weakness is manageable by protecting Skarmory and using Aegislash Shield form to absorb Fire hits.

Fire coverage is my top remaining need and Chandelure is the best value Fire-type on the board — 145 SpA with Flash Fire to absorb opposing Fire moves aimed at my Steel-types (Gholdengo, Excadrill). At 6 points it leaves 8 for my final 3 picks, keeping budget flexibility for a priority user and utility mon.

Metagross is exceptional value at 6 points and gives this roster its needed Steel-type defensive backbone into opposing Fairy pressure, especially Primarina, Grimmsnarl, and potential Mega Floette mirrors. Clear Body also makes it a reliable answer into the league’s many Intimidate users, while Bullet Punch provides valuable priority for the fast offensive matchups.

Altaria is an excellent one-point utility pick: Cloud Nine directly disrupts both the opposing rain core and the sun roster, while Tailwind, Helping Hand, Haze, and Perish Song give it several viable support modes. Its Dragon/Flying typing also provides a Ground immunity for Archaludon and Sneasler, improving positioning without committing the team to a single speed mode.
Forretress costs just 1 point, leaving 10 points for the final 3 picks, and provides invaluable steel utility, hazard stacking, and physical bulk to support the rain team.

Meowstic-Female gives the roster unusually valuable low-cost flexibility: Fake Out, Prankster-independent utility, Trick Room, Helping Hand, dual screens, Thunder Wave, and Yawn. It complements both Farigiraf/Armarouge slower modes and Altaria/Sneasler faster modes while adding a second strong support Psychic without consuming a Mega slot.

Hisuian Goodra is an exceptional 6-point fit: its Steel/Dragon typing and 150 base SpD give the roster a durable special pivot that complements the physically sturdy Garchomp, Metagross, and Milotic. Sap Sipper also creates a valuable Grass immunity for the Water- and Ground-oriented core, while it remains usable in either Tailwind or Trick Room compositions.

Vaporeon's Water Absorb is critical insurance for Tyranitar (4x Water weak) and Excadrill (2x Water weak), especially against P5's rain core and P3's Milotic. Wish + Protect gives team healing that keeps my sand core healthy, and Ice Beam threatens the Garchomp and Dragonite running around. At 5 points it leaves exactly 3 for two final picks, where 1-pt options like Absol (Sucker Punch priority) or Houndoom (Flash Fire) can round out the bench.

Swampert at 6 points is the most efficient Ground-type pivot still available. Water/Ground typing gives me crucial Electric immunity to protect Charizard and Torkoal, while providing excellent coverage alongside my Sun core. It can run U-turn for momentum, Stealth Rock, Earthquake, and Ice Beam, filling the team's biggest remaining hole.

Gliscor (3) fills the glaring Ground-type gap in my roster — I currently have zero Ground coverage into Gholdengo, Aegislash, and Archaludon. Poison Heal makes it a status-absorbing defensive pivot that synergises perfectly with my Steel-heavy core (Mega Metagross, Klefki, Corviknight), while its Electric immunity protects Rotom-Wash from Volt Switch spam. At 95 base Speed it outspeeds most defensive mons and can run Toxic/Roost/Earthquake/Protect sets that my bulky offense desperately needs.

Clawitzer (4 pts) is the ideal special wallbreaker for this roster. Mega Launcher boosts Water Pulse, Dark Pulse, Aura Sphere, and Dragon Pulse to 90–127 BP off 120 base SpA, giving me SE coverage into Steels (Aura Sphere), Ghosts/Dragons (Dark/Dragon Pulse), and Fires (Water Pulse). It also brings Flip Turn for pivoting and rounds out my special attacking core alongside Dragapult and Rotom-Wash. Leaves exactly 1 point for Dedenne as the final pick.

Spiritomb (Ghost/Dark, 6 pts) is the best available special wall and directly addresses the Psychic/Ghost/Dark coverage gap. Its 108/108 special defenses, Pressure for PP stall, and Infiltrator to bypass screens make it a premier pick. It resists Psychic, Ghost, and Dark, and is immune to Normal and Fighting—covering key threats from Farigiraf, Mega Gengar, Dragapult, and Hatterene. Leaves 3 points for Scrafty as a Fighting/Dark physical attacker with Moxie and Intimidate.

Absol at 1 point gives me a Sucker Punch priority user for revenge killing fast threats like Sneasler, Dragapult, and Basculegion, plus a Dark STAB option against opposing Ghosts and Psychics. Justified is a niche bonus if opponents target it with Dark moves. This leaves 2 points for my final pick, where 2-pt options like Qwilfish (Intimidate+Swift Swim) or Sandaconda (Sand Spit synergy with Tyranitar) remain available.

Scrafty gives the roster a vital cheap VGC utility package in Intimidate, Fake Out, and Dark/Fighting coverage, while functioning well under either Talonflame Tailwind or Hatterene Trick Room. It also helps our Steel- and Psychic-heavy core into Ghost- and Dark-type pressure without committing our primary Mega choice.

Qwilfish is the best remaining 2-point utility pick: Intimidate adds valuable physical control to a roster that otherwise lacks it, while Water/Poison patches several defensive gaps and gives useful disruption through options such as Taunt, Haze, and Nuzzle. Its decent Speed also lets it function as an active support piece rather than passive Intimidate fodder, and it can pressure the opposing rain core with Poison STAB.

We need to use our remaining 6 points across our final 2 picks, spending 5 points here on Alakazam (5) to add a fast special attacker/utility threat, leaving 1 point for our final selection. Alakazam provides incredible speed and high Special Attack to complement our rain core.

We have 1 point left and need our final 10th Pokémon to complete the draft. Castform costs exactly 1 point, matching our exact remaining budget. This fills our final roster slot legally and concludes our draft.

Dedenne is the best remaining 1-point fit, providing fast Nuzzle speed control, Electric/Fairy typing, and useful disruption alongside Qwilfish. Its support utility gives the roster another way to pressure faster teams without competing for the Mega slot or duplicating a major offensive role.

Mega Alakazam supplies the fast special offense the roster otherwise lacks, with 150 base Speed, 175 base Special Attack, and Trace creating strong matchup-specific utility. It also gives the team a legitimate alternate Mega option to Mega Floette, while Talonflame/Scrafty and Hatterene preserve flexible Tailwind and Trick Room modes.

Sandaconda rounds out my Tyranitar + Excadrill sand core as a backup Sand Spit setter, ensuring Excadrill's Sand Rush stays online even if Tyranitar is pressured or eliminated. Glare gives my team much-needed speed control outside of sand, Shed Skin provides a status absorber, and Coil + Body Press offers a late-game win condition from a fresh Ground typing that doesn't overlap with my existing types.

At 3 points, Heracross (Bug/Fighting) fills the critical Fighting-type gap that Scrafty was meant to cover. Guts boosts its Attack when statused, and Moxie snowballs after KOs. It hits Mega Metagross, Tyranitar, and other Dark/Rock threats for super-effective damage, while its Bug STAB pressures Psychic and Grass types that trouble the team.

Dedenne is already drafted by Luna-pro, so the private note's plan is void. Furfrou is the best remaining 1-point option: Fur Coat doubles its physical Defense, making it a legitimate bulky pivot at base 102 Speed. It brings Thunder Wave for speed control, U-turn for momentum, and a Ghost immunity that helps against Mega Gengar and Dragapult — unique utility none of the other 1-point leftovers can match.

builds.rationale: Opponent brings a Drizzle rain core (Pelipper + Swift Swim Mega Swampert/Basculegion) backed by Prankster Whimsicott and Primarina. Serperior is the hard counter to every Water-type, OHKOing Mega Swampert and threatening Basculegion/Primarina after one Contrary boost. Rotom-Wash OHKOs Pelipper with Volt Switch before it can Hurricane, and burns physical Swift Swim sweepers. Incineroar provides Fake Out + Intimidate cycling to disrupt their tempo. Klefki sets dual screens behind Light Clay to blunt rain-boosted attacks; Thunder Wave neutralises Swift Swim speed. Mega Metagross deletes Whimsicott with any Steel move and trades favourably into Primarina. Corviknight offers Tailwind to match their speed tier and a sturdy Flying/Steel pivot that walls non-Water attacks.

We bring a rain core featuring Pelipper, Mega Swampert, and Basculegion-Male, supported by Whimsicott for Tailwind, Primarina for bulky special offense, and Mega Ampharos to pressure Rotom-Wash, Corviknight, and other defensive pivots. Pelipper sets rain immediately so Mega Swampert and Basculegion can outspeed and overwhelm threats like Mega Metagross and Incineroar under Swift Swim.

Sun team anchored by Charizard Y and Torkoal Drought+Heat Rock. Venusaur's Chlorophyll pushes its Speed past 200 in sun, turning Growth-boosted Giga Drain and Sludge Bomb into an overwhelming sweep. Aegislash is completely immune to Psychic (Ghost typing) and walls Farigiraf and Armarouge for free, while Sacred Sword and King's Rock flinch pressure handle physical threats. Meowscarada's Protean gives STAB on every move, making it a fast mixed revenge killer and cleaner. Skarmory lays Stealth Rock (4× against Mamoswine) and Spikes, provides a Defog-resistant physical wall with Sturdy, and Whirlwinds out setup.

Cloud Nine Altaria suppresses Mega Charizard Y's sun while setting Tailwind, and Armarouge's Wide Guard protects the team from Heat Wave and other spread attacks. Mamoswine pressures Charizard, Torkoal, Toxapex, Aegislash, and Skarmory with its Ground-, Ice-, and Rock-type coverage, while Archaludon provides strong special damage into the Fire- and Flying-heavy core. Dedenne and Sneasler add speed control, disruption, Fake Out, Quick Guard, and Helping Hand support for flexible four-Pokémon selections.

The opponent's two Mega options define the matchup: Mega Floette (Fairy Aura Moonblast at 102 Spe) and Mega Alakazam (175 SpA at 150 Spe, Trace). I bring the Sand core (Tyranitar + Excadrill) for speed control—Excadrill at 308 in sand outspeeds everything—plus Gholdengo as the defensive anchor resisting Fairy, Psychic, and Dragon simultaneously. Mega Gengar traps and eliminates weakened targets with Shadow Tag while resisting Fairy. Grimmsnarl provides Prankster screens and Spirit Break to neuter special attackers. Tauros rounds out with Intimidate and 4x-effective Close Combat on Hisuian Goodra. Key defensive wins: Tyranitar is immune to Psychic (hard-walls Alakazam), Gholdengo tanks Floette's Moonblast for 19-59%, and Tyranitar's Rock Slide is a guaranteed OHKO on Talonflame.

Mega Floette is the primary closer against their Dark-, Water-, and Fighting-type options, while Garchomp supplies immediate pressure into Tyranitar, Excadrill, and Gholdengo. Talonflame Tailwind and Milotic Icy Wind give two ways to deny Mega Gengar and Sand Rush Excadrill their speed advantage; Scrafty disrupts special attackers with Snarl and Intimidate, while Metagross checks Grimmsnarl and can pick off Mega Gengar with Bullet Punch. Favor Talonflame + Metagross or Talonflame + Garchomp leads when early Tailwind is safe, and preserve Floette until their Steel- and Poison-type pressure is contained.

This six uses a flexible Trick Room mode through Farigiraf and Armarouge, while Sneasler and the faster investment on Archaludon provide immediate pressure outside Trick Room. Mamoswine targets Mega Metagross, Incineroar, Gliscor, Serperior, and Dragapult, while Armarouge's Wide Guard protects against likely spread attacks and Sinistcha supplies redirection, healing, and sustain. Armor Tail, Fake Out, Taunt, and Helping Hand give the team strong control over the opponent's priority and setup options.

Klefki sets Prankster screens + Thunder Wave to control Sneasler's speed and blunt Armarouge's special output. Incineroar cycles Intimidate onto Sneasler/Mamoswine while Darkest Lariat threatens Farigiraf. Dragapult (213 Spe) outspeeds and OHKOs Sneasler with Life Orb Psychic Fangs. Clawitzer's Mega Launcher + Expert Belt Aura Sphere and Dark Pulse break Archaludon and Farigiraf. Mega Metagross cleans late-game with Tough Claws-boosted STABs once threats are paralysed or removed. Rotom-Wash spreads burns and pivots with Volt Switch.

Use Talonflame and Manectric to punish the Pelipper rain lead: priority Tailwind preserves speed control while Lightning Rod can redirect targeted Water- and Electric-type attacks. Mega Floette is the primary breaker, with Energy Ball pressuring Mega Swampert and Fairy Aura-boosted Fairy attacks covering Basculegion, Whimsicott, and Mega Ampharos. Hatterene plus the slow Scrafty/Hisui Goodra core gives a second Trick Room mode that is especially strong into Swift Swim teams.

We correct the EV allocations to ensure no stat exceeds 32 Stat Points under the Champions format while keeping our powerful rain core intact. Pelipper sets rain for Mega Swampert and Basculegion, Whimsicott provides fast Prankster support, Primarina acts as a bulky special pivot, and Mega Ampharos breaks through bulky walls with Mold Breaker.

The opponent's scariest archetype is sun (Mega Charizard Y + Torkoal + Chlorophyll Venusaur), so Tyranitar's Sand Stream is the backbone — it overrides Drought, neuters Fire damage, and activates Excadrill's Sand Rush for a sweeper that outspeeds the entire format. Mega Gengar at 200 Speed outspeeds max Jolly Meowscarada and likely OHKOs with Sludge Bomb, while Shadow Tag traps Toxapex/Aegislash for cleanup. Grimmsnarl provides Prankster screens + Fake Out for safe leads, and Spirit Break is the team's only SE hit into Spiritomb while softening Charizard Y's SpA. Tauros-Aqua brings Intimidate, Water STAB to delete the Fire types, and a Fighting resist to wall Heracross. Gholdengo rounds out with Steel/Ghost typing (resists Grass/Poison/Bug, immune to Fighting), Make It Rain spread damage, and Good as Gold to block status — but must stay away from Charizard Y until sand is firmly set.

Sun offense anchored by dual Drought setters (Charizard Y and Torkoal) to power Fire moves and unlock Venusaur's Chlorophyll speed. Aegislash is the critical Ghost-type answer to Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag, immune to trapping while threatening Gholdengo with super-effective Shadow Ball. Heracross provides Fighting/Bug coverage with Moxie snowball, demolishing Tyranitar and Excadrill at 4x and 2x respectively, plus Vacuum Wave priority. Skarmory is the physical wall, setting Spikes and using Whirlwind to phaze setup sweepers. Venusaur exploits Chlorophyll speed in sun to spread Sleep Powder (shutting down Gengar's Shadow Tag) while firing instant Solar Beam and Sludge Bomb for coverage.

Klefki sets Prankster Light Screen/Reflect to neuter Fairy Aura-boosted attacks and protect Dragapult from Mega Alakazam's Shadow Ball. Mega Metagross is the primary breaker — Jolly 178 Speed outruns both Mega Floette and Garchomp, OHKOing the former with Meteor Mash. Dragapult cleans Psychic-types with Life Orb Shadow Ball and nukes Garchomp with Draco Meteor, but needs Tailwind or screens before facing Mega Alakazam. Incineroar provides Intimidate cycling and Fake Out disruption (avoid Parting Shot into Hatterene). Rotom-Wash burns physical threats like Garchomp and pivots with Volt Switch. Corviknight supplies Tailwind, a second Steel/Fairy resist, and Mirror Armor to reflect Scrafty's Intimidate.

Mega Floette is the primary breaker for Dragapult and Incineroar, while Garchomp and Goodra pressure their Steel/Electric core from complementary angles. Talonflame supplies reliable Tailwind, Scrafty disrupts leads with Fake Out and Snarl, and Competitive Milotic punishes Incineroar while checking Gliscor and providing Icy Wind insurance.

This six targets the opponent’s sand and spread-damage core with Mamoswine’s Ground/Ice pressure, Armarouge’s Wide Guard, and Archaludon’s strong special Steel/Dragon attacks. Farigiraf blocks opposing priority and can reverse the speed matchup with Trick Room, while Sneasler and Dedenne provide fast disruption against Mega Gengar, Grimmsnarl, and the slower sand attackers. Flash Fire Armarouge is also a safe pivot into Chandelure, while Thick Fat Mamoswine improves the matchup into Fire- and Ice-based coverage.

The opponent's biggest threat is Unburden Sneasler (base 120, doubled after item pop), which guaranteed-OHKOs Tyranitar with 4x-SE Close Combat. Gholdengo is the perfect counter: immune to both Fighting and Poison STABs while also resisting Archaludon's Dragon/Steel STABs. Sand core (Tyranitar + Excadrill) provides speed control and Rock Slide flinch pressure into Armarouge/Altaria; Excadrill runs High Horsepower over Earthquake to avoid chunking Gholdengo/Tyranitar allies and still threatens possible OHKOs on Archaludon and Sneasler. Mega Gengar at 200 Speed outspeeds the entire roster pre-Unburden and uses Taunt to shut down Farigiraf Trick Room and Sinistcha recovery. Grimmsnarl Prankster screens plus Spirit Break neuters the opponent's special attackers. Tauros-Aqua Intimidate plus Expert Belt delivers possible OHKOs on Mamoswine (Close Combat) and Armarouge (Wave Crash) while softening physical hits team-wide.

The opponent brings a prominent sun core with Mega Charizard Y and Torkoal, alongside Chlorophyll Venusaur and physical threats like Meowscarada and Heracross. We deploy a rain team anchored by Pelipper's Drizzle to override their sun and empower our water attackers. Mega Swampert abuses rain with Swift Swim to dismantle Charizard, Torkoal, and Venusaur, while Basculegion and Primarina clean up defensive walls like Toxapex and Aegislash. Whimsicott provides crucial speed control via Tailwind and Prankster support, and Forretress sets hazards and handles physical attackers.

Opponent is running a rain core with Mega Swampert, Basculegion, and Pelipper backed by Mega Ampharos as a special breaker. My six pivot away from Sun to handle this: Toxapex with Regenerator and Rindo Berry is the primary Water and Ground check, Venusaur Calm-walls special Water/Ghost/Fairy pressure, Aegislash is the dedicated Mega Ampharos and Alakazam switch-in with 202 SpD and Expert Belt-boosted super-effective hits, Skarmory sets dual hazards and Whirlwind-phazes setup, Heracross with Moxie snowballs through Forretress and physical walls, and Protean Meowscarada with Choice Scarf at 190 Speed revenge-kills Alakazam and cleans late game.

Sand core (Tyranitar + Excadrill) provides ultimate speed control—Excadrill at 280 Spe under sand outspeeds Dragapult's 213 and everything else. Tyranitar's Helping Hand (+5 priority) turns Excadrill's High Horsepower into a reliable OHKO on Mega Metagross. Houndoom is the primary wallbreaker: Flamethrower OHKOs Metagross/Klefki/Corviknight, Dark Pulse OHKOs Dragapult, and Flash Fire lets it switch into Incineroar Fire moves aimed at Tyranitar. Mega Gengar traps and removes threats with Shadow Tag—Shadow Ball for Dragapult, Energy Ball as the team's only SE answer to Rotom-Wash, and Taunt to shut down Klefki/Rotom-Wash status. Gholdengo's Good as Gold blocks Prankster TWave and WoW while Shadow Ball hits Metagross SE via Psychic weakness. Tauros provides Intimidate support and Close Combat to remove Incineroar.

Mega Gengar (130 Spe, 170 SpA, Shadow Tag) is the centerpiece with Grimmsnarl screens + Tyranitar/Excadrill sand. Dragapult outspeeds Gengar and threatens OHKO with Life Orb Shadow Ball. Rotom-Wash walls Excadrill (Iron Head 10-12%) and threatens Hydro Pump KOs on both sand members. Incineroar cycles Intimidate with Fake Out + Parting Shot, Chople Berry lets it eat Tauros-Aqua Close Combat. Mega Metagross Tough Claws Psychic Fangs guarantees OHKO on Gengar; Bullet Punch cleans weakened threats. Klefki matches Grimmsnarl's screens with Light Clay. Serperior snowballs with Contrary Leaf Storm into Tyranitar, Excadrill, and Tauros-Aqua.

Opponent leans on hyper-offensive Megas (Alakazam 150 Spe, Mega Floette 155 SpA) and strong physical threats (Garchomp, Scrafty). Our six answer with three pillars: (1) hazard pressure via Glimmora Stealth Rock/Spikes/Toxic Debris and Skarmory Spikes to wear everything down; (2) priority and speed control — Palafin Hero-form Aqua Jet, Mimikyu and Aegislash Shadow Sneak, plus Skarmory Tailwind to let our whole team outrun 150 Spe; (3) dedicated Fairy and Psychic checks — Mimikyu SD Play Rough deletes Mega Floette and shreds Hatterene, Aegislash's Steel typing tanks Psychic and Fairy STAB while King's Shield cripples physical attackers, and Toxapex Regenerator absorbs Garchomp's Earthquakes and provides a Haze safety net. Win condition is Palafin Flip Turn into Hero form sweeping after hazards stack.

Use Talonflame/Garchomp to force a fast Tailwind mode, while Scrafty/Hatterene gives a credible Fake Out + Trick Room pivot into Torkoal and slower Water/Steel structures. Mega Floette is the primary cleaner and keeps Energy Ball specifically for Swampert; Milotic is the long-game Palafin and physical-Water answer. Preserve Talonflame’s Sash and Scrafty’s Fake Out pressure to deny opposing Trick Room or create the turn Floette needs to Mega safely.

We bring a dominant rain team featuring Pelipper, Mega Swampert, and Basculegion-Male, supported by Whimsicott, Primarina, and Mega Ampharos. Every Pokémon follows the Champions format EV caps strictly: exactly 66 total Stat Points per Pokémon, with no single stat exceeding 32 points (distributed across multiple stats like Atk, Def, SpA, SpD, and Spe to avoid hitting >32 in HP, Def, SpA, or Spe).

Cloud Nine Altaria suppresses Pelipper's rain while providing Tailwind, letting the team answer Swift Swim threats without committing to Trick Room. Mamoswine's Freeze-Dry and Archaludon's Thunderbolt pressure the Water core, while Sinistcha redirects attacks and sustains the team; Sneasler supplies Fake Out, Quick Guard, and immediate pressure into Whimsicott, Alakazam, and Forretress. Dedenne adds Nuzzle speed control and Eerie Impulse support against Primarina, Mega Ampharos, and other special attackers.

Rotom-Wash walls Palafin's Jet Punch (0.25x in sun with Water resist) and threatens OHKO with Thunderbolt. Dragapult outspeeds the entire opposing roster and pressures Palafin/Aegislash/Mimikyu with Life Orb coverage. Serperior's Contrary Leaf Storm snowballs while OHKOing Swampert and threatening Palafin. Incineroar cycles Intimidate + Fake Out to neuter Meowscarada and Mimikyu, with Flare Blitz OHKOing Meowscarada. Mega Metagross provides Tough Claws Bullet Punch priority to break Mimikyu's Disguise and clean weakened targets. Gliscor punishes Glimmora's Toxic Spikes via Poison Heal and threatens the Torkoal/Glimmora/Toxapex core with Expert Belt Earthquake.

This team dismantles the opponent's core of Mega Metagross, Dragapult, and Incineroar through layered offense, sturdy pivoting, and hazard attrition. Palafin and Mimikyu form a potent sweeper pair—Palafin flips into Hero form for devastating Close Combat and Waterfall, while Mimikyu's Disguise plus Focus Sash guarantees a safe Swords Dance or Play Rough hit to destroy Dragapult and Incineroar. Toxapex and Aegislash anchor the defense, walling physical threats with Regenerator recovery and King's Shield attack-drops while punishing with Liquidation burns and Shadow Ball. Glimmora lays Stealth Rock and Spikes with Lum Berry for status protection, and Toxic Debris passively punishes special attackers. Meowscarada's Protean and 192 base Speed let it revenge-kill anything with a guaranteed-STAB move—Flower Trick crits Corviknight, Dark Pulse obliterates Dragapult, Energy Ball OHKOs Rotom-Wash, and Brick Break pressures Mega Metagross.

Opponent runs a rain core (Pelipper Drizzle + Mega Swampert/Basculegion Swift Swim) with Whimsicott Prankster support and Primarina as a special nuke. Tyranitar's Sand Stream immediately overrides rain, shutting down Swift Swim speed doubling; Excadrill at 280 Spe under Sand Rush outspeeds their entire roster and sweeps with Rock Slide spread + Iron Head for Fairies. Gengar-Mega at 200 Spe traps with Shadow Tag post-Mega and OHKOs Pelipper (Thunderbolt 4x), while Sludge Bomb and Shadow Ball threaten Primarina and Basculegion respectively. Grimmsnarl's Dark typing makes it immune to Whimsicott's Prankster moves, and Prankster Taunt shuts down their setup; dual screens help the frail sweepers survive. Hydrapple resists Water and possibly OHKOs Mega Swampert with 4x SE Giga Drain, pivoting with Regenerator. Gholdengo's Steel/Ghost typing gives it a 4x Ghost resist into Basculegion while Good as Gold blocks all status moves.

The opponent brings a potent sand core in Tyranitar and Excadrill alongside Gholdengo, Grimmsnarl, Mega Gengar, and Paldean Tauros (Aqua). We establish a robust rain team featuring Pelipper, Mega Swampert, Basculegion, Primarina, Whimsicott, and Forretress to flip the weather, outspeed sand rush under rain, and break through their defensive backbones.

Bring both Mega options: Mega Alakazam is the primary anti-Trick Room and Sneasler answer, while Mega Floette is the preferred Tailwind endgame when Steel- and Poison-types are contained. Talonflame plus Scrafty create early tempo with Tailwind, Taunt, Fake Out, and Intimidate; Garchomp pressures Archaludon and Armarouge, while Competitive Milotic punishes Qwilfish Intimidate and can Haze away Stamina boosts. Preserve Floette and Milotic carefully against Mamoswine, and use Alakazam's Taunt rather than priority disruption when Farigiraf is on the field.

This six combines Altaria's Cloud Nine and Tailwind with immediate pressure from Mamoswine, Armarouge, and Archaludon, covering weather, Garchomp, Metagross, Floette, Hatterene, and Milotic without depending on Trick Room or Wide Guard. Farigiraf denies opposing priority and Imprisons Trick Room while providing Helping Hand support, and Scarf Sneasler gives a fast answer to Mega Alakazam and Scrafty. Yache Mamoswine and Flash Fire Armarouge improve the Talonflame/Garchomp matchup while the combination of Thunderbolt, Energy Ball, and Grass coverage prevents Milotic from being safely ignored.

offers.message: Proposing a 1-for-1 swap: Mega Charizard Y (20) for Mega Floette (20). Mega Charizard Y's mega stone has been expended and it can no longer mega-evolve, leaving a dead slot on my roster. Mega Floette brings powerful Fairy STAB via Moonblast, Flower Veil to block status on allies in doubles, and Symbiosis for creative item support. At 20 points each, the trade keeps both rosters at budget.
offers.offerReasoning: Mega Charizard Y is expended and unusable in future games, creating a critical dead slot on a 10-Pokemon roster. Sun has been consistently shut down by Cloud Nine and Sand Stream across all three matches, so pivoting away from sun dependency is essential. Mega Floette fills the slot with a usable Pokemon whose Fairy STAB (Moonblast) pressures Dragons and Dark types, Flower Veil provides doubles support, and Symbiosis enables item-passing strategies. Hazard removal remains the top priority for the next trade phase.
offers.responseReasoning: With its Mega Stone expended, Charizard Y effectively becomes a much weaker base Charizard and would overlap heavily with Talonflame’s Fire/Flying role. Mega Floette is a premier special Fairy with 155 SpA, 148 SpD, 102 Speed, and Fairy Aura, so trading it for an unusable mega slot is a substantial downgrade.

offers.offerReasoning: No trade is sufficiently attractive at mid-season. The roster is already budget-maxed, so most upgrades would require an equal-cost exchange; the realistic options would sacrifice established tools such as Mamoswine's immediate weather pressure, Farigiraf's anti-priority and speed-control support, or Sneasler's disruption. Retaining the complete roster best preserves flexible matchup-specific sixes for the remaining opponents.

No equal-cost swap presents a clear upgrade over the current role compression. The roster already has distinct Mega Floette and Mega Alakazam modes, Talonflame/Hatterene dual speed control, and Scrafty/Milotic disruption; moving a low-cost glue piece would risk weakening those established lines more than it improves a matchup.

My current roster sits at a clean 100/100 points, featuring a potent rain core anchored by Pelipper, Mega Swampert, Basculegion, and Primarina, alongside supportive and utility pieces like Whimsicott, Alakazam, Forretress, Mega Ampharos, and Feraligatr. Having gone 2-1 and successfully ironing out my rain strategies and anti-rain checks, holding my roster gives me stability as I prepare for the regular season.

offers.message: Straight 1-for-1 swap: I get Altaria for its Ground immunity and Water resist to patch my sand team's biggest holes. In return you get Absol — Sucker Punch, Feint, and Shadow Sneak give you priority that actually works under Trick Room (unlike Altaria's Tailwind which is anti-synergy with your TR setup). Absol also brings Knock Off, Taunt, and Close Combat as fast utility under TR. Clean lateral move for both of us.
offers.offerReasoning: Altaria (Dragon/Flying) is immune to Ground and resists Water — my team's two biggest weaknesses with zero current Ground resists and 4 Water-weak mons. It adds Tailwind speed control, Roost recovery, Will-O-Wisp, and Natural Cure utility. I only lose Absol's niche Sucker Punch priority, which Grimmsnarl's Dark typing already partially covers. Entrant 4 runs TR where Altaria's Tailwind is anti-synergy, making Absol's TR-friendly priority more useful to them.
offers.responseReasoning: Altaria provides the roster’s only Ground immunity, along with valuable Water resistance and Cloud Nine utility against weather, which helps protect Archaludon and Armarouge. Absol’s priority and Taunt are useful, but its poor bulk and limited defensive value make it a much less reliable Trick Room support piece; the claimed priority advantage does not compensate for losing Altaria’s unique resistances and Helping Hand access.

offers.offerReasoning: My 3-0 roster has no exploitable weaknesses and every slot pulls its weight. The only mathematically legal trades (Clawitzer↔Ampharos-Mega at 4pts, or Furfrou↔any 1pt mon) are sidegrades at best. Ampharos-Mega is slow and redundant with Rotom-Wash/Dragapult; no 1-point free agent or owned mon matches Furfrou's Fur Coat utility. Both remaining opponents (Sun and Sand+Shadow Tag) are already well-covered by my existing anti-sun core and Dragapult/Rotom-Wash respectively.

moves.reasoning: Dropping the entire sun core (Charizard-Mega Y, Venusaur) and low-value Heracross to pivot away from sun offense, which lost all three games. Glimmora provides automatic Toxic Spikes via Toxic Debris plus Stealth Rock/Spikes/Corrosion for Gholdengo coverage. Mimikyu's Disguise + Swords Dance + Play Rough gives a non-sun win condition and a direct Fairy-type answer to Gholdengo. Palafin's Zero to Hero + Jet Punch priority is a powerful rain/sand-neutral threat that doesn't depend on weather. Skarmory stays for Defog, keeping hazard control intact. Budget: 13+11+12=36 added, 20+13+3=36 dropped.

I am making no trades. The current roster already preserves the Archaludon/Mamoswine/Armarouge offensive shell, Altaria's Cloud Nine and Tailwind, and the supporting tools needed for redirection, recovery, disruption, Nuzzle, and speed-control denial. No available free agent improves the Rotom-Wash, Mega Gengar, sun, and sand matchups broadly enough to justify sacrificing one of these established roles.

The current 100-point roster already has distinct, matchup-relevant modes: Mega Floette endgames, Life Orb Garchomp pressure, Talonflame Tailwind, Hatterene Trick Room, and Mega Alakazam speed offense. No available free agent improves those roles enough to justify losing the established anti-sand, anti-rain, and anti-Metagross coverage supplied by the current ten.

Sitting at 3rd place with a 2-1 record and a strong, fully-synergized rain core (Pelipper, Mega Swampert, Basculegion, Primarina, Whimsicott), our roster is already at the 100/100 budget cap and performing excellently. Our series reflections and wins highlight that our current team handles physical pivots and defensive archetypes with ease, so keeping our current roster intact for the regular season is our best path forward.

Three targeted upgrades: Hydrapple replaces Chandelure with a Water/Ground-resistant Regenerator pivot (Giga Drain 4x SE on Swampert-Mega, Earth Power 2x SE on Metagross-Mega) — critical for the rain matchup while still hitting Steel types. Houndoom replaces the dead-weight Absol at equal cost with Dark/Fire typing, Flash Fire immunity, and Flamethrower/Heat Wave coverage (2x SE on Klefki). Rotom replaces Sandaconda with Levitate Ground immunity — the team's biggest structural hole — while adding Electric STAB (4x SE on Pelipper) and Ghost typing for the spam core.

The 3-0 roster is balanced, type-diverse, and has verified answers for both remaining opponents. Furfrou's Ghost immunity is specifically valuable into Mega Gengar (Week 5), and no 1-point alternative offers comparable role compression. Clawitzer's Mega Launcher-boosted special Water offense fills a unique niche that Rotom-Wash's defensive pivot set doesn't cover. Standing pat preserves proven synergy.

builds.rationale: Same rain matchup we beat 2-0 in Week 1. Serperior is the hard counter to every Water-type, OHKOing Mega Swampert and threatening Basculegion/Primarina after one Contrary boost. Rotom-Wash walls Water attacks (Waterfall 28-47%, Wave Crash 52-77%), OHKOs Pelipper with Volt Switch, and burns physical Swift Swim sweepers. Incineroar provides Fake Out + Intimidate cycling to disrupt their tempo. Klefki sets dual screens behind Light Clay to blunt rain-boosted attacks; Thunder Wave neutralises Swift Swim speed. Mega Metagross deletes Whimsicott with Steel STAB and cleans with Bullet Punch. Corviknight offers Tailwind to match their speed tier and walls Whimsicott completely. Opponent may adapt with Mega Ampharos or Alakazam, but the core plan remains sound — remove Pelipper early, paralyse the Swift Swim sweepers, and let Serperior snowball.

We bring our dedicated rain core of Pelipper, Mega Swampert, and Basculegion-Male, alongside Whimsicott, Primarina, and Mega Ampharos. Every Pokémon strictly adheres to the Champions format rule: at most 32 points in any single stat and at most 66 total points across the spread. Pelipper sets rain immediately to give Mega Swampert and Basculegion overwhelming Swift Swim speed and power against Incineroar and Mega Metagross, while Mega Ampharos and Primarina pressure defensive pivots like Rotom-Wash and Serperior.

Register both Mega options: Mega Alakazam is the clean immediate answer to Mega Gengar, while Mega Floette is the preferred endgame when Gengar and Gholdengo are contained. Garchomp pressures the revealed sand/Steel core, Talonflame supplies Tailwind and Grimmsnarl disruption, and Scrafty plus Competitive Milotic provide the Intimidate, Snarl, and Icy Wind insurance needed against their alternate physical and special modes.

This is a rematch against an opponent who beat me 1-2 in week 1 using Fake Out Scrafty + Mega Floette leads with Garchomp Life Orb EQ as the primary win condition. I bring the Sand core (Tyranitar + Excadrill) for speed control—Excadrill at 140 Spe under sand outspeeds Floette-Mega, Garchomp, and Manectric while Rock Slide threatens Talonflame (4x) and Iron Head threatens Floette (2x). Mega Gengar at 200 Spe outspeeds the entire roster except Alakazam-Mega and can OHKO Floette-Mega with Sludge Bomb (53-109%), Hatterene with Sludge Bomb (62-202%), and Alakazam-Mega with Shadow Ball (64-148%). Gholdengo is the defensive anchor: Steel/Ghost resists Fairy (NVE from Floette's Light of Ruin at 27-87%), immune to Fighting (Scrafty Drain Punch), and resists Psychic (Alakazam-Mega Psychic at 15-46%). Grimmsnarl runs Adamant for Spirit Break OHKO potential on Garchomp (47-102%) and Scrafty through Roseli Berry (52-113%), with Prankster dual screens to keep Tyranitar alive against Garchomp EQ (39-68% under Reflect) and Scrafty Drain Punch (35-66% under Reflect). Rotom provides Levitate Ground immunity to switch into Garchomp EQ freely, Thunderbolt for Talonflame (43-158%) and Milotic (28-89%), Will-O-Wisp to neuter Garchomp/Scrafty/Metagross, and Thunder Wave for speed control on Floette-Mega and Alakazam-Mega.

Dragapult is Ghost-type and immune to Shadow Tag, letting it pivot freely and threaten Mega Gengar with Life Orb Shadow Ball (75–138% roll). Rotom-Wash walls Excadrill completely (Iron Head 10–12%) and Volt Switches out of trapping while 2HKOing Tyranitar through sand. Klefki sets Prankster screens to blunt sand-boosted Rock Slides and Thunder Waves Gengar to neutralise its speed. Incineroar cycles Intimidate + Fake Out with Chople Berry to eat Tauros-Aqua Close Combat; Darkest Lariat ignores Grimmsnarl screens. Corviknight provides Tailwind to match Excadrill's Sand Rush and Mirror Armor reflects opposing Intimidate. Mega Metagross cleans late with Tough Claws Psychic Fangs (guaranteed OHKO on Gengar), Meteor Mash OHKO on Grimmsnarl, and Bullet Punch priority for chipped Excadrill.

Rematch against deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro (won 2-0 in week 4 with this same six). Sand core (Tyranitar + Excadrill) provides ultimate speed control — Excadrill at 280 Spe under sand outspeeds Dragapult's 213 and everything else. Houndoom is the primary wallbreaker: Flamethrower OHKOs Klefki and threatens Metagross-Mega/Corviknight, Dark Pulse OHKOs Dragapult, and Flash Fire switches into Incineroar's Fire moves. Mega Gengar traps with Shadow Tag post-Mega, Shadow Ball OHKOs Dragapult/Metagross, Energy Ball is the only SE answer to Rotom-Wash, and Taunt shuts down Klefki/Rotom-Wash status. Gholdengo's Good as Gold blocks all Prankster status from Klefki while Shadow Ball hits Dragapult/Metagross SE; Dazzling Gleam replaces Make It Rain for better spread coverage into Dragapult. Tauros provides Intimidate to weaken Metagross/Incineroar, Wave Crash handles Incineroar through Chople Berry and Gliscor if adapted in, and Close Combat removes Furfrou/Incineroar.

decisions.rationale: Incineroar + Rotom-Wash lead: Fake Out (+3) flinches Whimsicott before Prankster Tailwind, while Volt Switch guarantees OHKO on Pelipper and pivots into Serperior. Intimidate weakens physical Swift Swim sweepers. Serperior enters safely and threatens every Water-type with Contrary Leaf Storm. Mega Metagross in back handles Whimsicott (Steel→Fairy) and Primarina, with Bullet Punch priority to finish Sashed targets.

Bring Pelipper and Swampert as our starting lead to immediately establish Drizzle rain and unleash Mega Swampert's Swift Swim speed and power. Back them up with Basculegion to clean up with Choice Scarf Swift Swim and Whimsicott for Prankster Tailwind support if speed control needs refreshing.

Fake Out Pelipper prevents Tailwind and Weather Ball; Volt Switch guarantees OHKO on Pelipper (131–260%) and pivots into Serperior. Swampert may Mega Evolve and attack Incineroar, but Focus Sash ensures survival. Serperior then threatens Swampert with a guaranteed Leaf Storm OHKO next turn. Removing Pelipper early denies Tailwind and limits rain resets, while preserving momentum with the Volt Switch pivot.

Both Pelipper and Swampert protect on turn 1 to scout the opponent's moves (such as Fake Out from Incineroar and potential Hydro Pump or Volt Switch from Rotom-Wash) while ensuring Swampert safely Mega Evolves and gains Swift Swim under Rain.

Parting Shot Swampert-Mega to stack -2 Atk while pivoting to Serperior, Volt Switch Pelipper for the guaranteed OHKO and a pivot. Swampert moves first but Incineroar lives any single hit with Sash; even if double-targeted and Pelipper wins the speed tie, the worst case is trading Incineroar for Pelipper plus Serperior vs -1 Swampert. Serperior OHKOs Swampert with Leaf Storm next turn.

Serperior OHKOs Mega Swampert with Leaf Storm and survives any single hit from the opponent's likely attackers (Ice Punch 41-59%, Wave Crash 43-63%, Moonblast 30-48%). Even if Swampert outspeeds in rain, Serperior tanks the hit and KOs back, gaining a +2 SpA Contrary boost. Incineroar at 1% stays in as a sacrifice to absorb one attack, protecting Serperior from being doubled. Metagross is preserved in back for later.

Incineroar must switch after Parting Shot. Rotom-Wash is the optimal switch: Levitate grants immunity to Swampert-Mega's Earthquake, it resists Waterfall and Ice Punch, and it provides a pivot with Volt Switch against potential Basculegion or Primarina switches. Metagross takes neutral from both Earthquake and Waterfall and lacks recovery. Serperior stays in; Leaf Storm is a guaranteed OHKO on Swampert-Mega, forcing the opponent to Protect or switch, both of which give us momentum.

Pelipper uses Weather Ball into Incineroar (super-effective in rain, taking out or heavily damaging Incineroar) and Swampert-Mega uses Waterfall into Incineroar or Rotom-Wash (Waterfall into Incineroar ensures a KO or high damage). Since Incineroar used Fake Out last turn and cannot use it again, and Rotom-Wash used Volt Switch last turn (likely switching or attacking Pelipper's slot, but Pelipper is threatening Incineroar while Swampert outspeeds and hits hard), doubling into Incineroar is safe and pressures the opponent immediately.

Pelipper fainted last turn, so we must replace it. Bringing in Basculegion under rain gives us a strong Swift Swim physical attacker with Wave Crash and Last Respects, while Swampert-Mega passes its turn to accommodate the replacement switch.

Serperior Leaf Storm OHKOs Swampert-Mega guaranteed (145.9-252.6%) and gains +2 SpA via Contrary, snowballing into a win condition. Rotom-Wash Volt Switch damages Basculegion (45.8-86.2%) and pivots for momentum. Basculegion moves first but cannot OHKO Serperior alone (Wave Crash 42.7-62.7%; Last Respects ~48-72% at 100 BP). Swampert may Protect, but if it does Leaf Storm is merely blocked while Volt Switch still connects. Worst case double-target on Serperior with Swampert winning the speed tie has only a partial KO chance; the upside of removing Mega Swampert and boosting Serperior is decisive.

Rotom must switch after Volt Switch. Switching to Incineroar triggers Intimidate, dropping Swampert to -3 Atk and Basculegion to -1 Atk, which helps Serperior survive future turns. Serperior uses Protect to guarantee survival this turn. If Incineroar is KO'd (likely), Metagross enters for free without taking a hit. If Incineroar survives, it threatens Fake Out next turn. Either way, Serperior is preserved to OHKO Swampert with Leaf Storm next turn and snowball with Contrary.

Basculegion outspeeds everything with Swift Swim and Choice Scarf, so Last Respects hits Serperior cleanly. Swampert-Mega protects against Serperior's Leaf Storm or Rotom's moves while Basculegion attacks.

Incineroar Fake Out (priority +3) flinches Swampert-Mega before it moves, preventing Ice Punch or Earthquake chip that could combine with Last Respects to KO Serperior. Basculegion is locked into Last Respects and deals 16.7–24% to Serperior, leaving it at 8–15.3%. Serperior then Leaf Storms Basculegion for a guaranteed KO from 13% and gains +2 SpA via Contrary. End state: Incineroar 1%, Serperior 8–15.3% +2 SpA vs Swampert-Mega 100% -3 Atk -1 SpA, with Metagross and Rotom-Wash in back. Even if Swampert Protects, it wastes its turn and Basculegion still falls.

Switch Metagross into Incineroar's slot; Mega Evolve on entry for Tough Claws. Serperior stays in and should Leaf Storm Swampert-Mega. Swampert-Mega is choice-locked into staying (opponent's only remaining bench Pokémon replaces Basculegion). Leaf Storm is a guaranteed OHKO even from 89% HP and gives +2 SpA via Contrary. Speed order Serperior (181) vs Swampert (180–244) is uncertain, but the risk/reward favors attacking: if Serperior moves first, Swampert faints and Serperior reaches +4 SpA — a winning position. If Swampert moves first and Ice Punches Serperior, Serperior falls but Metagross-Mega enters safely and faces a -3 Atk Swampert whose Earthquake does only 27–38% while Zen Headbutt (Tough Claws boosted ~33–58%) 2HKOs back. Rotom-Wash is preserved in the back as a Levitate pivot immune to Swampert's Ground moves.

Basculegion outspeeds both opponents under rain and Swift Swim and easily KOs the 1% Incineroar with Last Respects. Swampert-Mega can target Serperior with Waterfall to secure major damage or a KO, or we can use Swampert appropriately. Since Incineroar has 1% HP, hitting it with Last Respects is a guaranteed KO while freeing Swampert to pressure Serperior.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Switch Serperior out to preserve it; switches resolve before moves so Serperior escapes safely. Mega Evolve Metagross for Tough Claws and Bullet Punch Whimsicott to break Focus Sash. Whimsicott's Prankster Tailwind goes first but can't stop the switch or Bullet Punch. Rotom-Wash enters immune to Swampert's Earthquake and resists Ice Punch (4.5–9.6%). Next turn Metagross-Mega Bullet Punch KOs the 1 HP Whimsicott, leaving a 2v1 against a -3 Atk Swampert with Serperior still in reserve.

Whimsicott outspeeds both opponents and can use Moonblast on Serperior to finish off its remaining 22% HP (or Encore it). Swampert-Mega can use Ice Punch on Serperior to secure the KO if Moonblast rolls low, while Whimsicott handles Serperior directly.

Bullet Punch (+1 priority) breaks Whimsicott's Focus Sash, leaving it at 1 HP. Volt Switch then KOs the 1 HP Whimsicott and pivots Rotom-Wash to Serperior. Swampert-Mega at -3 Atk cannot threaten either slot meaningfully (EQ into Metagross 25-35%, Ice Punch into Rotom 6-8%). Even if Whimsicott Protects, we lose little; if it Encores, the target still executes its planned move and Volt Switch still KOs. Next turn Serperior Leaf Storm OHKOs Swampert-Mega for the game.

Whimsicott Protects to shield itself from Metagross's Bullet Punch or Rotom's attack. Swampert-Mega uses Earthquake, which hits both opposing Metagross and Rotom (Levitate applies to Rotom? Wait, Rotom has Levitate so Earthquake misses Rotom, but hits Metagross-Mega super effectively). Let's check Swampert's Earthquake into Metagross-Mega and Whimsicott Protect.

Bullet Punch from Metagross is a guaranteed OHKO on the 31% Whimsicott (50.3–97.8%) and its +1 priority ties Prankster Tailwind/Encore, preventing Whimsicott from safely setting up. Hydro Pump from Rotom into Swampert-Mega deals 47.8–82.3%, leaving it in easy cleanup range for Serperior's Leaf Storm next turn. Swampert's -3 Atk Earthquake only does 24.5–34.8% to Metagross and cannot KO Rotom (immune). Even if Whimsicott's 1/3 Protect succeeds, the board remains strongly in our favour.

Whimsicott uses Protect to shield itself from Metagross-Mega's priority Bullet Punch (and potential Rotom-Wash attacks), while Mega Swampert uses Earthquake to deal heavy super-effective spread damage to Metagross-Mega (and hit Rotom-Wash, bypassing its Levitate immunity).

Swampert-Mega is the last foe at 7% HP. Bullet Punch (+1 priority) is a guaranteed OHKO and outspeeds all Swampert attacks except Protect. Hydro Pump is backup: if Protect succeeds (low odds on 3rd consecutive use), both moves are blocked but Swampert wastes its turn, and we go to turn 9 with rain expired, Metagross faster, and Protect even less reliable. If Protect fails, Bullet Punch KOs and the game ends.
Swampert-Mega uses Earthquake to hit Metagross-Mega super effectively while Whimsicott is fainted.

reflections.summary: We won by removing Pelipper on turn 2, denying permanent rain and Swift Swim, then stacking Intimidate and Parting Shot to reduce Swampert-Mega to -3 Attack. This made Swampert’s Earthquakes weak and allowed Rotom-Wash and Metagross-Mega to clean up safely, with Serperior preserved as a backup threat.
reflections.adjustment: Next game, expect the opponent to protect Pelipper more carefully or lead Whimsicott to set Tailwind early. Consider leading Incineroar + Serperior to pressure Swampert immediately, and be cautious of Whimsicott’s Encore locking us into Protect or setup moves.

reflections.summary: The opponent successfully neutralized Pelipper early with Volt Switch and controlled momentum with Incineroar's Parting Shot and Fake Out cycles, while Serperior and Metagross-Mega dismantled our offensive core.
reflections.adjustment: Bring Whimsicott earlier or position Tailwind safely to outspeed the opponent's backline before being overwhelmed by priority moves.

decisions.rationale: Lead Incineroar + Serperior for immediate pressure. Incineroar's Fake Out (priority +3) stops Whimsicott's Prankster Tailwind/Encore or Basculegion's attack. Serperior's Leaf Storm OHKOs Swampert (168-302%), threatens Basculegion (86-156% 2× SE), and pressures Pelipper (59-118%). Contrary + Life Orb turns Leaf Storm into a snowballing +2 SpA boost. Rotom-Wash in back punishes rain with Electric STAB and burns physical attackers; Metagross-Mega cleans late with Tough Claws Bullet Punch and Zen Headbutt. Klefki and Corviknight sit out — Whimsicott's Prankster Encore punishes Klefki's status moves, and Corviknight fears Ampharos-Mega's Electric STAB.
Pelipper sets Drizzle for Swift Swim Swampert and Basculegion while bringing Tailwind or heavy offenses, with Whimsicott in the back for speed control and utility.

Fake Out Pelipper stops Tailwind, the opponent's most dangerous turn-1 play. Leaf Storm into Swampert is a guaranteed OHKO if it stays in and doesn't Protect; if it Protects, Contrary gives Serperior +2 SpA anyway. If they switch Swampert to Whimsicott, Leaf Storm chips through Sash and we handle it next turn; if Basculegion comes in, it risks a high-roll OHKO. Stopping Tailwind while pressuring the Swift Swim sweeper is the highest-value line.
Both Pelipper and Swampert protect on turn 1 to waste Fake Out from Incineroar and dodge any potential damage from Serperior while allowing Swampert to Mega Evolve safely.

Switch Incineroar to Rotom-Wash (resists Water, immune to Ground via Levitate, takes only 17-38% from Waterfall and 21-50% from Weather Ball). Serperior Leaf Storm OHKOs Swampert-Mega (145-252%) before or between foe attacks — even if Swampert is faster, Ice Punch only does 41-58% and Serperior still KOs back. Rotom-Wash safely absorbs any attacks aimed at Incineroar's slot. If Swampert Protects, Rotom-Wash is still in a strong position and we preserve Serperior.

Rotom-Wash dominates Pelipper with 4x Volt Switch and resists both its attacks; no reason to forfeit. Switching Incineroar into the fainted Serperior slot: Incineroar resists Basculegion's Ghost STAB (Last Respects 0.5x) while Metagross is 2x weak to it, and Intimidate cycling neuters Basculegion's physical Wave Crash/Last Respects. Fake Out also provides disruption next turn. Metagross-Mega is better preserved for later after Basculegion is handled.
Swampert-Mega outspeeds both foes under Swift Swim and can KO Serperior with Ice Punch, while Pelipper targets Serperior with Hurricane to pressure it before it moves.
Swampert fainted last turn, so we must replace it. Basculegion enters under Rain, threatening massive damage with Swift Swim active, while Pelipper remains on the field.

Volt Switch OHKOs Pelipper through any non-Protect action while Fake Out (+3 priority) flinches Pelipper before it can move. Basculegion attacks in between (Wave Crash into Incineroar triggers Focus Sash at 1 HP; into Rotom-Wash does 26-38% which is safe). After Volt Switch KO, Rotom pivots to Metagross. Result: Pelipper removed, Basculegion Choice-locked, Metagross in safely, rain persists but their setter is gone. Even if Pelipper Protects, we only lose one turn of momentum—but they must also predict perfectly.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Pelipper sets Tailwind to outspeed any potential Speed control or fast threats like Mega Metagross, while Basculegion hits Incineroar super-effectively with Wave Crash in the rain for a guaranteed KO.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.
